DefinitionQuery.description: Text to find in a report name, description or ManageEngine name. Plain text only; no filter syntax.
DefinitionQuery.name: q

DefinitionVersion.description: A published version of the definition. Absent answers the current one.
DefinitionVersion.name: version

IdempotencyKey.description: Makes a mutating bulk call safe to retry. The same key with a different body is refused.
IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key

IfMatch.description: The ETag of the version being changed; a stale value answers precondition-failed.
IfMatch.name: If-Match

OperationId.description: The operation to undo: the value of the ActiveDIQ-Operation-Id header that the Action-backed write answered.
OperationId.name: operationId

PageCursor.description: The nextCursor of the previous page.
PageCursor.name: cursor

RequiredIdempotencyKey.description: The request ID. It names the audit events of the change and makes a retry of a create safe.
RequiredIdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key

RequiredIfMatch.description: The ETag of the schedule version being changed. A stale value answers precondition-failed; an absent one precondition-required.
RequiredIfMatch.name: If-Match

RunDefinitionFilter.description: Only runs of this report definition.
RunDefinitionFilter.name: definitionId

ScheduleOwner.description: me lists the caller's schedules. any lists every schedule of the tenant and needs reports.schedule.manage_all.
ScheduleOwner.name: owner

SortBy.description: A column of the run to sort the stored result by. Absent keeps the run order.
SortBy.name: sortBy

SortOrder.description: The sort direction. Absent is ascending.
SortOrder.name: order

example.title: The object already exists or the request conflicts

Conflict.description: The object already exists or the request conflicts

example.title: The directory refused our service account

DirectoryAccessDenied.description: The directory refused our service account

example.title: You are not allowed to do this

Forbidden.description: You are not allowed to do this

example.title: The idempotency key was used with a different request

IdempotencyKeyReuse.description: The idempotency key was used with a different request

NotImplemented.description: The operation is declared but not built yet

NotReady.description: The service is running but not ready to take traffic

OperationNotUndoable.description: The operation cannot be undone; errors[].code says why (irreversible, already_undone, superseded, not_finished, tier0_blocked, plan_refused)

example.title: The password does not meet the policy

PasswordPolicyViolation.description: The password does not meet the policy

example.title: The request body is too large

PayloadTooLarge.description: The request body is too large

ReportResultExpired.description: The stored result or file has expired

example.title: The result is over the row cap of the format

ReportRowCapExceeded.description: The result is over the row cap of the format

example.title: The scope covers no directory objects

ReportScopeEmpty.description: The scope covers no directory objects

example.title: The scope uses a kind that reports cannot evaluate

ReportScopeUnsupported.description: The scope uses a kind that reports cannot evaluate

example.title: The search text cannot be used

SearchQueryInvalid.description: The search text or cursor cannot be used. errors[].code says why: query_too_short (empty after normalisation), query_too_long (over 256 characters), query_invalid (NUL or invalid UTF-8), query_refused (the text looks like a 48-digit BitLocker recovery password: refused without echoing, logging or tracing it; the same answer whatever the digits), cursor_invalid (bad, forged or mismatched cursor), cursor_requires_type. Neither detail nor errors ever repeat the text.

example.detail: Search could not finish. Try again, or narrow the text.
example.title: Search is unavailable

SearchUnavailable.description: Search could not finish in time

SetupRefused.description: First-run setup was not claimed. One answer for every cause (wrong secret, expired secret, secret already used, install not in first-run state), so the response teaches a caller nothing. It never carries a detail.

SignInFailed.description: The sign-in did not succeed. One answer for every cause (unknown account, wrong secret, non-local account, disabled account, throttled account, expired or exhausted pending sign-in), so the response teaches a caller nothing (TM section 7.6 rule 2). It never carries a detail.

example.title: A fresh multi-factor check is required

StepUpRequired.description: A fresh multi-factor check is required

AssignmentGrant.description: Input of delegation.assignment.grant. The caller chooses assignmentId, so a retry is the same grant. A role holding a control_plane permission is granted to an account only.

AssignmentRevoke.description: Input of delegation.assignment.revoke. Ends one assignment; a revoked assignment is not restored.

AssignmentRoot.description: One scope root of an assignment (DM-35). exclude subtracts the subtree from the scope.

AssignmentRootKind.description: What the root's guid names. The server refuses a kind it does not know.

AssignmentSubject.description: Who holds the assignment, by kind. Exactly the members of its kind are accepted.

BreakGlassPasswordRequest.description: The local break-glass account and its password.

CsrfValue.description: Which header carries the CSRF value and what it is. Named value, not token, because it is not a credential.

Cursor.description: An opaque page cursor. Clients pass it back unchanged.

DelegationId.description: A caller-chosen identifier of a role or an assignment, a canonical UUID.

DelegationPermissions.description: Permission names, each of the form family.noun.verb. Duplicates are collapsed.

DirectorySearchChip.description: One status chip of a hit. kind says which; at or days carry its value when it has one.

at.description: When it happened or will happen (locked, accountExpires, deleted).

DirectorySearchChipKind.description: One status of the object, as the IA 5.3 chips show it. at is present for locked, accountExpires and deleted when the time is known; days is present for passwordExpiresInDays. There is no free-form status text: the client words every chip.

DirectorySearchDisambiguator.description: What tells two objects with one name apart. Each member is present only when the inventory holds it; the client joins what is there (title, then office or department).

DirectorySearchGroup.description: The permitted hits of one type. count, more and nextCursor describe only objects the caller may read; none of them can be used to infer what the scope hides. Under refine, count, more and nextCursor are all absent.

count.description: How many objects of this type the caller may see for this text: the trimmed result, never a total over the directory. Absent when the normalised text has under 3 characters, and when refine is true.

limitReached.description: True when paging stopped at 1,000 permitted hits. The client shows "refine your search"; there is no further cursor. The stop depends only on permitted hits.

more.description: True when the caller may see more hits than items holds. A flag, never a number. Absent when refine is true.

nextCursor.description: Pass back with the same q and type to get the next page. Absent on the last page, and when refine is true.

DirectorySearchHighlight.description: A matched stretch of one field, counted in Unicode code points from the start of the field's value (not UTF-16 units, not bytes). A hit that matched on a key the row does not show (a SID, say) has no highlight.

DirectorySearchHighlightField.description: The field of the hit a highlight range refers to.

DirectorySearchHit.description: One permitted object, with everything a row shows. objectId is the key; distinguishedName is an attribute for display and may change when the object moves.

domain.description: The DNS name of the object's domain. The client shows it when the answer spans more than one.

status.description: Status chips, most urgent first. Empty when none applies.

DirectorySearchMatchClass.description: How the hit matched, best first. An object appears once, in its best class.

DirectorySearchObjectType.description: The kind of object a group or a hit is. The group order of a full answer is users, groups, computers, contacts.

DirectorySearchRequest.description: The search. q is typed text and never a filter. type narrows to one kind of object; it is required with a cursor.

groupLimit.description: The most hits per group; 5 when absent. With a cursor it is the page size.

q.description: The text to find, as the admin typed it: a name, a logon name, a UPN or e-mail, a SID, a GUID, a DN or a host name. Up to 256 characters. Never sent in a URL.

DirectorySearchResult.description: The grouped, permitted hits of one search, with the freshness of the inventory behind them.

asOf.description: When the inventory behind this answer was last synced (the oldest of the connections the caller may read). The search reads the inventory, not the live directory. Null when nothing has synced yet.

groups.description: One group per requested type, in the order users, groups, computers, contacts, even when a group is empty.

refine.description: True when the text is too broad to rank. No group then carries a count, a more flag or a cursor. The same for every caller with the same permissions.

DirectorySearchType.description: The kind of object to search. Without it all four are searched.

DirectoryUser.description: A user as search shows it. Only these fields; the objectGuid is the key.

GUIDRef.description: A reference to a directory object by objectGUID. A DN is never a key.

HealthState.description: ok is the only value; a probe that is not ok is a problem response, not a body.

HealthStatus.description: The only thing a health probe says.

HybridClassification.description: How the user stands in the cross-directory correlation (DM-20) under TM-D17, computed from the stored correlation and the Entra connection's takeover protection. not_hybrid: no correlation is recorded. candidate, matched, broken: the strongest recorded state (matched over candidate over broken). unknown: the facts could not be read; treat as no authority. Only a matched correlation can carry authority, and only while takeover protection is attested and neither side is Tier 0.

reason.description: Why the correlation is not matched, or why a matched one carries no authority. A stable code, never a directory value.

Int64String.description: A 64-bit integer carried as a string, for values outside JavaScript's safe integer range.

Job.description: A long operation (bulk change). It reports progress and per-item results, and is resumable after a restart.

JobStatus.description: Where a long-running operation is. Clients accept values they do not know.

ObjectView.description: A directory object as the server shows it. dn is for display only.

OperationChange.description: One changed field. field is the camelCase member path in the target's resource schema. before is absent when the field is set for the first time or the target is created; after is absent when it is removed or the target deleted. (The dialect allows only primitive nullables, so absence is a variant of OperationValue, not null.)

OperationConfirmation.description: One confirmation the caller gives after reading the preview. items repeats, exactly, the items of the requiredConfirmations entry of the same kind.

OperationConfirmationKind.description: What the caller confirms. A closed request enum.

OperationConfirmationKindValue.description: A confirmation the submit needs. external_recipients is "Data leaves your organisation". Clients accept values they do not know, and a client that does not know a kind cannot submit.

OperationHoldReasonValue.description: Why an operation is held for approval (ADR-0005 rule 8), mirroring the kernel's HoldReason (internal/platform/operation/holds.go). step_up: the Action needs a fresh MFA and the initiator cannot give one (an API token or an automation, TM-D30 SX-4); an approval that carries step-up releases it. blast_radius: an automation touches more objects than its limit. irreversible: the tenant requires approval for irreversible changes. undo_needed_approval: the undo of an operation that itself needed approval. gate: the registered approval gate asked for it. none: not held. (The dialect has no nullable $ref, so "not held" is a value, as HoldNone is in the kernel.) Clients accept values they do not know.

OperationPreview.description: What submitting the previewed request would do now. holdReason is the hold the submit would get when outcome is needs_approval, and none otherwise. stepUpRequired is true when the submit needs a fresh MFA (TM-D30 SX-1): an interactive caller without one is answered 401 step-up-required, and a token or automation is held step_up.

OperationPreviewOutcome.description: What submitting this exact request would do now: ready, no_change, needs_approval (ADR-0005 rule 8), refused (a step is blocked or the gate denies). Clients accept values they do not know.

OperationRef.description: An operation as a write answers it. holdReason says why a held (awaiting_approval) operation waits, so a client can tell an approval that carries step-up from a policy approval; it is none when the operation is not held.

OperationReversibilityValue.description: How far an undo restores the before-state (ADR-0005 rule 1). Clients accept values they do not know.

OperationStateValue.description: An operation's state (ADR-0005 rule 3, DM-41). Clients accept values they do not know.

OperationUndoRequest.description: Starts the undo of an operation. confirmations carries every confirmation the undo preview listed in requiredConfirmations; an empty list when it listed none.

OperationValue.description: One side of a change, rendered by the Action for display. redacted stands for a secret or an erased personal value.

PageInfo.description: Cursor paging of a directory collection. Order is stable; nextCursor is null on the last page.

Problem.description: An RFC 9457 problem. type is a relative reference, /problems/<slug>, from a closed catalogue.

ProblemDirectory.description: The directory's own result, with secrets stripped. Never raw LDAP text with internals.

ProblemError.description: One violation. pointer is a JSON Pointer inside the body, or the parameter name.

item.description: For a bulk request, the index of the item the violation belongs to.

Rdn.description: One relative distinguished name component, unescaped, for breadcrumbs.

ReportCategory.description: The six categories of the 2a library (spec 6.1).

ReportCategoryValue.description: A library category. Clients accept values they do not know.

ReportCell.description: One typed cell; the kinds map one to one onto report.Cell in modules/reports.md 6.2 (text s, integer i, boolean b, time t, enum e, guid g, textList l, absent a, never n, unknown u). unknown is shown rather than an inferred value when an input is missing (FR-09). absent is a missing value, distinct from empty text; never is a value that cannot occur, such as a last logon of an account that has never logged on.

ReportCellGuid.description: An object GUID or other GUID attribute, canonical lower-case.

ReportCellInteger.description: A whole number as a decimal string, so 64-bit directory values stay exact.

ReportCellNever.description: The value can never exist for this object, as distinct from absent (not yet set).

ReportCellText.description: Text as stored in the directory, which may hold any character. Encoders neutralise it on export.

ReportCellTextList.description: A multi-valued text attribute, in stored order.

ReportCellUnknown.description: A derived state whose input is missing (Unknown (input missing)).

ReportChoice.description: One value of an enum column: a stable ID and its label.

ReportColumnId.description: A column of the dataset registry (DM-70) that a 2a report carries. Closed: a column name that is not listed is refused, and a column the chosen definition does not carry is a 400 with code column_not_available. The registry holds no secret attribute (D8).

ReportColumnInfo.description: A column of a definition, or of one run (a label can change with the run, such as Last logon (at least)). filterOperators are the operators the column takes.

ReportColumnTypeValue.description: What a column holds, which decides the operators it takes.

ReportCompareOperator.description: A comparison of one column with one typed value. contains and starts_with are literal text matches: no wildcard or pattern character has a meaning.

ReportDcCoverage.description: How many DCs answered a per-DC report. A partial coverage makes the maximum a lower bound (spec 6.5).

ReportDefinition.description: A report definition: an immutable AST over one registered dataset (FR-03, FR-05), shown as its presets, crosswalk and columns. exportFormats are the formats this installation can produce, and the console offers no others. subjectKind says whether the report requires groups or users (GRP-02, GRP-03). minScheduleIntervalHours is 24 for per-DC reports.

ReportDeliveryReason.description: Why a delivery failed. external_not_permitted: the owner no longer holds reports.deliver.external. address_no_longer_allowed: the address left the allowed domains.

ReportDeliveryState.description: The delivery of the latest fire to one recipient.

ReportEmptyReason.description: Why a succeeded run has no rows because of scope, as opposed to its filters. scope_grants_nothing: the runner's role covers no directory objects. unsupported_scope_kind: the role's scope uses a kind 2a reports cannot evaluate, so it grants nothing (fail closed).

ReportExport.description: An export job and its stored file (DM-72.I3). When the run's result had expired, rerun is true, runId is the new run and rerunOfRunId the expired one; the file carries the new run's as_of.

ReportExportCreate.description: Starts an export of the run in the path.

ReportExportFormat.description: An export format. csv, xlsx, pdf and html all exist. A definition lists the formats this installation can produce for it: no pdf when the report has more columns than a PDF page lays out (24).

ReportFailure.description: A typed failure. message is fixed text; it names no object.

ReportFailureReason.description: A typed reason for a failed run or export, the set of run.FailureReason in modules/reports.md 6.2. runner_inactive: the runner's account is disabled or gone. token_refused: the token behind the run was revoked or expired. row_cap_exceeded: the result is over the row cap. per_dc_read_cap_exceeded: the per-DC read cap would be passed (spec 6.5). scope_too_large: the scope cannot be rendered within limits. query_timeout: the run passed its time limit. connection_unavailable: a connection could not be read (per-DC reads only). definition_retired: the definition was retired before the run started. interrupted: the run job was interrupted. internal: anything else.

ReportFilter.description: A typed filter tree over registry columns. A node names a column from the closed list and a typed value; there is no expression, no raw LDAP, no SQL. The tree is at most four levels deep and 64 nodes; deeper is a 400 with code filter_too_complex. The server checks each operator and value against the column's type.

ReportFilterCompare.description: One column compared with one value.

ReportFilterConditionView.description: One column, an operator and its values (none for has_value and empty).

ReportFilterIn.description: One column equal to any of up to 50 values.

ReportFilterMatch.description: How a group of filters combines: all (AND), any (OR) or none (NOT any).

ReportFilterMatchValue.description: How a group of filters combines.

ReportFilterOperatorValue.description: An operator a column takes, or one a preset's filter uses. within_last, within_next and older_than carry the number of days as one integer value.

ReportFilterPresence.description: A column has a value or is empty.

ReportFilterRelative.description: A time column relative to the start of the run.

ReportFilterView.description: A filter as the server stores it. A condition's column is a registry column ID.

ReportFreshness.description: The freshness label of spec 8.2. label is the text to show, such as Synced 09:41. When state is stale, stale names every naming context that makes it stale, oldest first: the connection (by id and display name), the naming context, why it is stale and when its last sync pass was. It is empty in every other state. thresholdSeconds is the staleness threshold the run was judged against; it is null when the run was judged against no connection. The console shows these and derives nothing from label.

ReportFreshnessState.description: The freshness label of spec 8.2. per_dc_read is the only state that may be called live.

ReportHiddenGroup.description: A set of rows the run counted and did not store, such as probable service accounts (E2). count is the number of hidden rows after scope trimming and is at least 1: a group with nothing hidden is not listed. label is the group's name in the report definition. locked is true when the report cannot show the group, so the console offers no Show control for it.

ReportLastRunOutcome.description: How the last fire ended. nothing_to_send is a run with no rows under notify-only-if-data.

ReportMeName.description: An exact ManageEngine report name and the preset that answers it (spec 6.2).

ReportOuRef.description: An organizational unit by connection and objectGUID, never by DN. oneLevel false includes the whole subtree.

ReportParametersView.description: What a run or schedule is over, as stored. Period, OU and subject references and values are the request shapes; columns and filters are shown as IDs.

ReportPausedReason.description: Why a schedule is paused. owner_disabled and owner_lost_permission are the owner-authority pauses of spec 8.4; reassigned waits for the new owner.

ReportPeriod.description: The period a report looks at. The server refuses a range whose to is not after from, or longer than ten years.

ReportPeriodLastDays.description: The last n days, ending when the run starts. The presets offer 7, 30, 90, 180 and 365.

ReportPresence.description: Whether a column has a value.

ReportPreset.description: A named set of filters, a period and a column set over a report (spec 6.1 rule 2). Each ManageEngine name is a preset.

ReportRecipientAccount.description: An activeDIQ account. asLink delivers a link only that account can download while signed in and holding reports.export; otherwise the file is attached.

ReportRecipientEmail.description: An e-mail address. Attachment only; a link is never offered for an address. An address outside the tenant's allowed recipient domains is external.

ReportRecipientEmailView.description: An e-mail recipient. external is judged against the allowed recipient domains now.

ReportRecurrence.description: When a schedule fires, in the schedule's time zone. The minimum interval is one hour (spec 8.4).

ReportRecurrenceCustomDays.description: From a start, repeating every n days.

ReportRecurrenceCustomHours.description: From a start, repeating every n hours.

ReportRecurrenceCustomMonths.description: From a start, repeating every n months.

ReportRecurrenceCustomWeeks.description: From a start, repeating every n weeks.

ReportRecurrenceDaily.description: Every day at a local time, HH:MM.

ReportRecurrenceHourly.description: Every n hours at the given minute.

ReportRecurrenceMonthlyDay.description: On a day of the month at a local time. A month without the day runs on its last day.

ReportRecurrenceMonthlyLastDay.description: On the last day of every month at a local time.

ReportRecurrenceWeekly.description: On weekdays (1 Monday to 7 Sunday) at a local time.

ReportRelativeTime.description: A time column relative to the time the run starts: within the last or next n days, or older than n days.

ReportRow.description: One row of a stored result. rowKey is the object GUID or edge key; cells follow the page's columns.

ReportRowPage.description: A page of a stored result. rowCount is the run's total after trimming.

ReportRun.description: The run record (DM-72). hiddenGroups lists the sets of rows counted and not stored; it is empty when nothing was hidden or the run has not succeeded. asOf is the oldest sync watermark among the covered naming contexts. rowCount, objectsChecked and digest are set when the run succeeds; both counts are after scope trimming. digest is the SHA-256 over the canonical form of the stored rows (spec 8.3). scopeApplied is the human-readable summary shown in the header.

ReportRunCreate.description: Starts a run. definitionVersion absent means the current version, which the run record then pins.

ReportRunList.description: A page of the caller's runs, newest first.

ReportRunParameters.description: What a run is over. Every member is optional; an absent one takes the preset's value, then the definition's default. connectionIds default to every connection the runner's scope reaches. The runner's scope always applies and can only narrow what is asked.

columns.description: The columns shown and exported, in order. Replaces the preset's columns when present.

filters.description: Combined with AND. Replaces the preset's filters when present.

includeReadOnlyDcs.description: Per-DC reports only (USR-04, PWD-03). Absent includes read-only DCs.

ReportRunState.description: Run states (spec 8.1): queued, running, then succeeded, failed or cancelled; a succeeded run becomes expired when its result is removed.

ReportRunStateFilter.description: The run states a history list can be narrowed to. The request twin of ReportRunState (ADR-0004 rule 2: a request enum is closed, its response twin is open).

ReportRunSummary.description: A run in the history list: the header fields that answer "what ran, when, how did it end". asOf is the oldest sync watermark among the covered naming contexts. rowCount is the count after scope trimming and is null while the run has not succeeded and whenever scopeCurrent is false. scopeCurrent is true when the caller's read scope now equals the scope the run was trimmed with; when false, opening the run answers 409 scope_changed_rerun and retryReportRun makes a new one.

ReportSchedule.description: A schedule (DM-73). Recipients receive what the owner can see, not what they can see. The ETag header is the version for If-Match.

ReportScheduleReassign.description: Hands a schedule to another account.

ReportScheduleState.description: active fires on its recurrence; paused does not.

ReportScheduleWrite.description: The writable settings of a schedule. It runs the report, preset, filters, columns and scope as saved, pinned to the definition version. confirmedExternal lists the external addresses the caller confirmed in the preview (Data leaves your organisation); it must equal the set of external recipients that are new or changed.

timeZone.description: An IANA time zone name, such as Europe/Berlin.

ReportSkipReason.description: Why a connection was left out of a run.

ReportStaleCause.description: Why a naming context makes a result stale. older_than_threshold: its last sync pass is older than the staleness threshold. resync_required: its change feed is unusable and a full resync is needed. paused: its sync is paused, or its connection is suspended.

ReportStaleSource.description: One naming context behind a stale result. connectionName is the connection's display name when the run was made; it is the connection id's text when the run record predates names. lastPassAt is the start of the last successful sync pass of the naming context and ageSeconds is its age when the run was made. cause says why it counts as stale.

ReportSubjectRef.description: A group or user a report is about (GRP-02, GRP-03), by connection and objectGUID.

ReportValue.description: A typed filter value. Never an expression.

ReportValueEnum.description: A stable ID from the column's choices, such as enabled or never_account_flag. The server checks it against the column.

ReportValueText.description: Text compared literally. Control characters are refused.

RoleCreate.description: Input of delegation.role.create. The caller chooses roleId, so a retry is the same role. A role is never deleted; empty it with delegation.role.update.

tier.description: 0 administers Tier-0 scope, 1 platform administration, 2 help desk.

RoleUpdate.description: Input of delegation.role.update. Replaces a custom role's permissions; a built-in role is refused.

SecretInput.description: A secret a client sends: a password, a token. It is write-only, never appears in a response, and is held in memory only as a secret.Secret that is destroyed after the request.

SetupClaimRequest.description: The one-time setup secret and the details of the first tenant owner.

SetupOwner.description: The first tenant owner's account details.

SiemDestination.description: A destination as stored. It never carries a credential.

tlsVerified.description: True when the server certificate is verified (transport tls).

SiemDestinationWrite.description: The writable settings of a destination.

host.description: A plain host name or IP address. No scheme, port or path.

plaintextOptIn.description: Must be true with transport tcp and false or absent with tls.

port.description: Absent takes 6514 for tls and 514 for tcp.

SiemTransport.description: The transport of a stored destination. Clients ignore values they do not know.

SiemTransportSetting.description: tls is RFC 5425 with certificate verification and is the default; tcp is plaintext and needs the opt-in. UDP is not offered.

SubjectAccount.description: A console account. The only kind that may hold a control_plane role.

SubjectAutomation.description: An automation policy. Never holds a control_plane role.

SubjectGroup.description: A directory group, by connection and objectGUID. Never holds a control_plane role.

TakeoverAttestationStart.description: Where the Global Administrator signs in.

TotpCodeRequest.description: A TOTP code from the account's authenticator.

WebAuthnAssertion.description: The authenticator's assertion, each field base64url (RFC 4648 section 5) without padding.

WebAuthnCredentialType.description: The credential type; public-key is the only one today.

WebAuthnUserVerification.description: Whether the authenticator must verify the user.

bearer.description: A scoped API token in the Authorization header. Credentials never travel in a query string.

csrfToken.description: Required with the session cookie on POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE. Bearer-token requests are exempt.
csrfToken.name: X-CSRF-Token

sessionCookie.description: The console session cookie (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict).
sessionCookie.name: __Host-adiq_session

info.description: The one public API of activeDIQ. The console, scripts, ITSM integrations and the PowerShell module all call these operations. There is one version, /api/v1, and it only grows.
info.title: activeDIQ API

post.description: The first factor of a local break-glass account (ADM-142). Success answers 204 and sets exactly one cookie, the pending-sign-in cookie (__Host-adiq_pending: HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict, Path=/, at most 5 minutes). The response carries no session, no token and no body. The cookie authorises nothing except the second-factor operations. Every failure has one shape, 401 /problems/sign-in-failed: unknown account, wrong password, non-local account, disabled account and throttled account are indistinguishable by status, body, headers and timing class (an unknown account still costs one password verification). A throttled account is delayed on the server, never locked (rule 3). The source-IP limiter may answer 429 with Retry-After, which does not depend on the account named. Refused on any hostname bound to AN-5 or AN-7, and outside the console source-CIDR allow-list, with the same 401.

204.description: The password step passed. Only the pending-sign-in cookie is set.

Set-Cookie.description: The pending-sign-in cookie, __Host-adiq_pending, and no other cookie.

get.description: Returns the value the console sends in the X-CSRF-Token header on every mutation. It is bound to the session, readable only with that session cookie, and not a credential: it authorises nothing alone.

200.description: The CSRF header name and value for this session.

get.summary: The CSRF value for the calling session

post.description: Revokes the calling session on the server and clears the session cookie. It acts only on the caller's own session. Needs the CSRF header like any cookie-session mutation.
Needs the pending-sign-in cookie. Success and failure behave as for verifyWebAuthnSignIn.

parameters.description: The pending-sign-in handle set by the first factor. It is read from this cookie only; a missing or repeated cookie answers the same 401 as any other sign-in failure.
parameters.name: __Host-adiq_pending

204.description: The second factor passed and a session exists.

Set-Cookie.description: Two lines: the new session cookie, __Host-adiq_session, and a clearing __Host-adiq_pending.

post.summary: Verify a TOTP code and create the session (AN-10)

post.description: Needs the pending-sign-in cookie from a first factor. Answers the WebAuthn request options for the account's enrolled credentials. A missing, expired, consumed or exhausted pending sign-in gets 401 /problems/sign-in-failed, the same as a wrong factor.

parameters.description: The pending-sign-in handle set by the first factor. It is read from this cookie only; a missing or repeated cookie answers the same 401 as any other sign-in failure.
parameters.name: __Host-adiq_pending

200.description: The WebAuthn request options for this pending sign-in.

post.description: Needs the pending-sign-in cookie. On success the pending sign-in is consumed, a new session is created with a new ID, and the response (204, no body) sets the session cookie and clears the pending cookie. Any failure is 401 /problems/sign-in-failed and counts against the pending sign-in's five attempts.

parameters.description: The pending-sign-in handle set by the first factor. It is read from this cookie only; a missing or repeated cookie answers the same 401 as any other sign-in failure.

get.description: The redirect URI of the attestation sign-in. No session or token is read: the single-use state issued by the start is the credential, and the tenant is the one the state names, used only to look the state up. A bad, expired or replayed state, a refused code, a token of another tenant and a failed read all answer the same 303 to the failed page, so the caller learns nothing about the cause (the cause is in the audit). Success answers 303 to the recorded page. The response carries no token and no directory value.

parameters.description: The state issued by the start.
parameters.name: state

parameters.description: The authorization code. Absent when the IdP reports an error.
parameters.name: code

parameters.description: The IdP error code, when the administrator declined or the IdP refused. Never echoed.
parameters.name: error

303.description: Redirect to the console page that shows the outcome

get.summary: Return from the IdP sign-in of a takeover-protection attestation (AN-11)

post.description: Starts the TM-D17 attestation of an Entra connection. The answer is the IdP sign-in URL (authorization code with PKCE, one delegated read-only scope, no offline access) at which a Global Administrator of that tenant signs in. The server then makes the one read of the tenant's sync features itself and discards the token. Needs a fresh step-up.

200.description: The sign-in URL for the Global Administrator

put.description: Sets attestation_max_age. A longer age widens the window in which a missed takeover-flag flip still counts as attested, so it needs the same permission and a fresh step-up as starting an attestation. The value is at most 90 days (7776000 seconds).
put.summary: Set how long an attestation stays valid

post.description:
Universal search (directory.search; IA 5.3, ADR-0011). Answers users, groups, computers and contacts whose name or identifier matches q, grouped by type, each group ranked (exact identifier, then prefix, then fuzzy; live before deleted, enabled before disabled) and already carrying what an admin needs to tell two objects apart: no second call is needed to render a row. The query travels in the POST body, never in a path or query string, so it stays out of URLs and access logs (ADR-0011 rule 15); this is a read, it changes nothing, and it needs no Idempotency-Key. q is typed text, not a filter: LDAP, SQL and wildcard syntax have no meaning and are never passed through. The server normalises q (Unicode NFKC, case folding) before matching.
Trimming comes before counting (LF-39, T-0875). Every hit, count, flag and cursor in the answer is computed from objects the caller is permitted to read under directory.read, and from nothing else. There is no total over the unscoped directory, and no field changes with what the scope hides. A group never says how many objects exist, only how many the caller may see, and a truncated group says so with the flag more instead of a number.
refine. When the text matches so many keys in the tenant that the server will not rank them (ADR-0011 rule 13), refine is true. The answer then carries no count, no more flag and no cursor on any group, so the client shows "Keep typing to narrow the search". Hits of a better match class than the one that overflowed are still returned (an exact identifier still finds its object). refine is the same for every caller who holds the same permissions, whatever their scope, so it is never a zero-result answer that a hidden OU could cause.
counts. A group's count is present only when the normalised q has at least 3 characters and refine is false. For a shorter q, a group shows its first hits and "Show all" with no number.
Show all. A group's nextCursor, passed back with the same q and type, pages that one group, 50 hits per page (groupLimit applies up to 50), in the same order, and stops at 1,000 permitted hits with limitReached true. A cursor is opaque and bound to the query, class set, type and the caller's scope; a cursor presented with anything else is refused with 400 and reads nothing. Pages re-run the search, so they can shift if the inventory changes in between.
Refusals. 400 (errors[].code): query_too_short (q is empty after normalisation), query_too_long (over 256 characters), query_invalid (a NUL or invalid UTF-8), query_refused (q looks like a 48-digit BitLocker recovery password; it is refused and never echoed, logged or traced), cursor_invalid (bad, forged or mismatched cursor), cursor_requires_type (a cursor without type). 403 when the caller lacks directory.read. 429 when the client is over its rate limit. 503 search-unavailable, with a trace ID and no count, when the search cannot finish in time. No refusal repeats q.

refineState.summary: Too broad to rank - no counts, no more flags, no cursor

truncatedGroup.summary: A truncated group says so with a flag; nextCursor continues it

twoPeopleOneName.summary: Two users who share a name are told apart without opening either

200.description: The groups, each trimmed to the caller's scope

get.description: Answers the users of the caller's tenant whose display name, sAMAccountName or userPrincipalName contains q, in a stable order, at most limit of them. q is plain text: the characters ( ) * \ & | = ! < > ~ and control characters are refused with a 400, as is a q longer than 256 characters. Nothing from q is ever placed in a directory query as syntax.

parameters.description: Text to find. Plain text only; no filter syntax.
parameters.name: q

parameters.description: The most users to answer. Defaults to 25.
parameters.name: limit

get.description: Answers 200 while the process can serve a request. Status only; it never reports a version, a configuration value or a dependency.
Answers 200 when the service can take traffic and the not-ready problem otherwise. Status only; it never names which dependency failed.
get.summary: Is the service ready to take traffic

get.description: Answers every destination of the tenant, oldest first. A tenant has a handful of destinations, so the list is not paged.

post.description: Creates a destination. The default transport is TLS with certificate verification; plaintext TCP needs transport tcp together with plaintextOptIn true, and the opt-in is audited. The Idempotency-Key is the request ID of the audit events and names the destination: a retry with the same key and body answers the destination already created and changes nothing, and the same key with a different body is refused.

put.description: Replaces the writable fields. The change redirects the SIEM stream, so it is audited with the previous and the new target. The Idempotency-Key is the request ID of the audit events; use a new key for each intended change. A key that already recorded an update is never applied twice: a replay with the same settings returns the current destination, with different settings it is a 422.
put.summary: Replace the settings of a SIEM syslog destination

get.description: Answers the report definitions the caller may run, in the order the library shows them (category, then name), a page at a time. q finds a report by its name, its description or any ManageEngine report name it answers (spec 6.2, "Also known as"); it is plain text and is never a filter. The 2a library is AD only, and objects in state deleted or purged are in no report.

Answers one definition with its presets, ManageEngine crosswalk, columns and the export formats this installation can produce. version selects an older published version; absent answers the current one. Definitions are immutable; a change publishes a new version (X7).

delete.description: Deletes the stored file before it expires (FR-20). Only the account that created it may (modules/reports.md 7.1); a recipient of a delivery of it may not, because other recipients were sent the same file. Anyone else gets 404. Deleting is bookkeeping, not an Action; it is audited as export deleted.

get.description: Answers the export job: state, format, row count, size, file name, digest and expiry. Poll while the state is queued or running.

Streams the stored file, only to an authenticated request that holds reports.export, by export ID; the server resolves the ID to the export record and only the record names the blob. Two paths (modules/reports.md 7.1, 7.2). Creator path: the caller is the account that created the export, and the run-read gate passes for its run (runner is the caller, current read scope equals the stored one), so a scope change stops downloads too; a changed scope answers 409 with errors[].code scope_changed_rerun. Delivery-link path: the caller is not the creator and is the recipient of a delivery link. The right comes from the delivery record (DM-84 Delivery) written when the schedule fired, whose source is this export and whose recipient is the caller's account. It never comes from the schedule's current recipient list, so a recipient removed from the schedule can still open what that fire sent them and nothing later. The server also re-checks that the caller currently holds reports.export and that the account is enabled. The recipient gets the stored owner-scope artefact byte for byte; the run-read gate (runner and scope) does not apply to the recipient, because the delivery record is the authority. Anyone else, with or without reports.export, gets 404 (401 when signed out). The bytes are exactly the owner-scope artefact an attachment would carry, so the digest matches. The content type and file name are those of the format; the name is built by the download-header encoder. Every download is audited with the downloading account. An expired file answers 410 report-result-expired.

Answers the runs the caller started, newest first (createdAt, then id as the tie-break, so the order is stable), a page at a time. This is the run history. A scheduled run belongs to the schedule's owner, so the owner sees it here and nobody else does. Another account's runs are not in the list and are not counted: a run is readable only by its runner (modules/reports.md 6.6 check 2), and reports.schedule.manage_all never lists or opens a run. state and definitionId narrow the list; both are typed values, never a filter string. An item is the run header without the parameters, the digest and the scope text; getReportRun answers those. The list does not apply the scope check of getReportRun (check 4), because one item out of date must not fail the page. Instead each item says scopeCurrent: true when the caller's read scope now equals the scope the run was trimmed with (6.6 check 4, evaluated once for the page). When scopeCurrent is false the item's rowCount is null, because a count taken under a scope the caller no longer holds is not shown; opening that run answers 409 scope_changed_rerun, and retryReportRun makes a new run under the current scope. An expired run is listed with state expired and no row count to open. After retention deletes a run record (6.2) it is in no list. Listing is a read of the caller's own bookkeeping; it is not audited per item.

200.description: A page of the caller's runs, newest first

post.description: Starts one run of a definition over one frozen set of inputs, as a job. A change of preset, filter, period, scope or columns is a new run; paging and sorting read the stored result of one run and never re-execute (spec 8.1). The runner's scope is applied inside the query, and counts are computed after trimming. A run is not an Action (ADR-0005 rule 10): it is system bookkeeping, audited as an event with row count and digest, never values. A scope that grants nothing, or uses a kind reports cannot evaluate (group_members, Entra kinds), is not an error: the run succeeds with no rows and the run header's emptyReason names why (spec 5, unhappy paths). Exporting from such a run is allowed (a record of what was found); only creating, updating or resuming a schedule from such a scope is refused, with report-scope-empty or report-scope-unsupported. Fields that are absent take the preset's value, then the definition's default. Reuse window (modules/reports.md 6.1 step 3, ADR-0010): when the same runner already started a run with the same query and the same applied-scope fingerprint in the last 60 seconds, and it is queued, running or succeeded, that run is returned instead of a new one, still 202 with the same shape. Reuse is a read and passes the same run-read gate as getReportRun. Job limit (step 5): a tenant with 4 runs and exports not yet finished answers 429 with errors[].code too_many_report_jobs (spec 8.3); retry when one finishes.

202.description: The run is accepted and queued

get.description: Answers the run record: state, as_of, the freshness label, row count, digest, scope applied, parameters and any failure. Poll this while the state is queued or running. Run-read gate (modules/reports.md 6.6, run.ReadAccess), in order: the run must belong to the caller (runner account equals the caller; the schedule's owner for a scheduled run), otherwise 404, which does not say whether the run exists; and the caller's current read scope must equal the scope the run was trimmed with, otherwise 409 with errors[].code scope_changed_rerun and the client creates a new run. A scope revoke or a narrower token therefore stops reads at once. reports.schedule.manage_all never opens a run. An expired run stays readable as a record with state expired; its rows are gone (ADR-0010). A failed run answers 200 with its state and failure.

post.description: Cancels a queued or running run (FR-11). Only the account that started the run may cancel it; anyone else gets 404. A run that already finished is answered unchanged. Cancelling is bookkeeping, not an Action.

Serialises the run's stored result (never a fresh query) into a file as an asynchronous job: the columns of the run, its filters, and all rows up to the format's cap (spec 8.3). Needs reports.export, bound as this operation's permission, and also reports.run, checked inside the operation before the run is looked up (403 if either is missing; modules/reports.md 6.6 check 1 and 7.1). Run-read gate (6.6, run.ReadAccess), in order: runner account equals the caller, otherwise 404; the caller's current read scope fingerprint equals the one stored with the run, otherwise 409 with errors[].code scope_changed_rerun (create a new run); the run has succeeded, otherwise 409 with run_not_ready or run_failed. An expired run is not refused here (see below). The three 409 codes are separate. Rows over a format's cap are refused with report-row-cap-exceeded, never truncated. A format this installation cannot produce is a 400 with code format_unavailable. If the run's result has expired, a new run is created first and the export says so (rerun true, rerunOfRunId); its file carries the new run's as_of. A run whose scope grants nothing or uses an unsupported kind is exported as a record of what was found, not refused (only schedules refuse such a scope). Exports and runs count together toward the tenant job limit: with 4 not yet finished the answer is 429 with errors[].code too_many_report_jobs. Exports are audited with actor and row count; an export is not an Action.

202.description: The export is accepted and queued

post.description: Creates a new run with the definition, version, preset and parameters stored with this one, and answers it as createReportRun does (202, ReportRun, rerunOf set to this run). The new run is computed under the caller's current read scope, not the old one, so a retry is how a run that answers 409 scope_changed_rerun, or whose result has expired, is made readable again. Relative periods are evaluated again against the new run's own now (FR-09); the stored result of this run is untouched. Only the account that started the run may retry it; anyone else, and a run that does not exist, get 404 without saying which (6.6 check 2). Allowed from succeeded, failed, cancelled and expired. A run that is queued or running is refused with 409 and errors[].code run_in_progress; poll it or cancel it instead. A retry goes through the same create path as createReportRun, so the 60 second reuse window applies (a second retry while the first is queued or running answers the first new run) and so does the tenant job limit (429 with errors[].code too_many_report_jobs). If the definition version was retired meanwhile, the new run fails with reason definition_retired, as it would for any run. A retry is not an Action (ADR-0005 rule 10): it is system bookkeeping, audited as a run event with row count and digest and the rerunOf run id. It carries no request body, so it has nothing to carry a client idempotency key for; a double submit is absorbed by the reuse window.

202.description: The new run is accepted and queued

get.description: Reads a page of the run's stored rows. Order is the run order, or sortBy with order, then the run order as the tie-break; the cursor is bound to the sort it was issued for and a cursor used with another sort is a 400. The total is the run's rowCount and is never a count over the rows. The result is stored and frozen (ADR-0010 rule 3): a page never reflects newer data. Cells of a derived state show unknown, never an inferred value (FR-09). Run-read gate (modules/reports.md 6.6, run.ReadAccess), in order: runner account equals the caller, otherwise 404; the run is not expired, otherwise 410 report-result-expired; the caller's current read scope fingerprint equals the one stored with the run, otherwise 409 with errors[].code scope_changed_rerun (the client creates a new run); the run has succeeded, otherwise 409 with errors[].code run_not_ready (queued or running) or run_failed (failed or cancelled, with the reason). The three 409 codes are separate and a client must branch on the code, not the status.
Answers the caller's own schedules. owner=any lists every schedule of the tenant and additionally needs reports.schedule.manage_all; without it the answer is 403.

post.description: Creates a recurring run plus delivery, pinned to the definition version (spec 8.4). Creating a schedule is an Action (ADR-0005 rule 10, reports.schedule.create): it runs inline, has a preview diff, the gate, audit and undo, and the external-recipient confirmation is part of its preview. Operation permission: reports.schedule. Any recipient outside the tenant's allowed recipient domains is external; delivering to one additionally needs reports.deliver.external, and the addresses must be listed in confirmedExternal ("Data leaves your organisation"), or the answer is 403 (with errors[].code external_not_permitted) or 400 (code external_not_confirmed). That second permission guards the external case only. Scheduled data is what the owner can see, not what a recipient can see. The owner's scope is checked now: report-scope-empty or report-scope-unsupported refuses a schedule that could never deliver. The name is unique per owner, so a retried create is a 400 with code name_taken and changes nothing. Preview it first with previewCreateReportSchedule (same body and parameters; nothing is written). The ActiveDIQ-Operation-Id it answers is the undo handle for undoReportScheduleOperation.

ActiveDIQ-Operation-Id.description: The operation that made this change. It is the undo handle for undoReportScheduleOperation.

202.description: Held for approval by the gate or a kernel hold (ADR-0005 rule 8); holdReason says which, for example step_up when a token or automation makes a change whose after-state has an external recipient (TM-D30 SX-1, SX-4). Nothing changed yet; it applies when approved

post.description: The dry run of undoing one reports.schedule.* operation (ADR-0004 rule 14): it plans the inverse, reports.schedule.restore, against the live schedule for the caller, with the checks of the transition it makes (modules/reports.md 8): undoing a pause resumes, so only the owner may (owner_only); undoing a reassignment needs reports.schedule.manage_all and leaves the schedule paused (lossy); restoring external recipients needs reports.deliver.external, lists them in requiredConfirmations and sets stepUpRequired (TM-D30 SX-1). A plan refusal is a 200 with outcome refused. It writes, persists and audits nothing. 404 when the operation is unknown, is not a reports.schedule.* operation, or its schedule is not visible to the caller. 409 operation-not-undoable when no inverse can be planned at all, errors[].code irreversible, already_undone, superseded (the schedule changed after this operation; undo the later change first) or not_finished.

Undoes one reports.schedule.* operation, named by the ActiveDIQ-Operation-Id its write answered (ADR-0004 rule 14, ADR-0005 rule 10). The undo is a new operation of the Action reports.schedule.restore, planned against the live schedule for the caller with the checks of the transition it makes, run inline, audited, and itself undoable. It restores the version before the operation: undoing a create archives the schedule, a delete restores it, an update restores the previous version, a pause resumes it (owner only), a resume pauses it, and a reassignment restores the previous owner with the schedule still paused. It sends nothing, and a fire that ran in between is not recalled. confirmations must repeat the requiredConfirmations of the undo preview (external recipients the undo restores); otherwise 400 with code external_not_confirmed. 403 when the inverse needs a permission the caller lacks (errors[].code external_not_permitted, owner_only, manage_all_required). 404 as for the preview. 409 operation-not-undoable with errors[].code irreversible, already_undone, superseded, not_finished or plan_refused (the scope refusals of create). Undoing an operation that itself needed approval is always held (202). Step-up (TM-D30 SX-1): undoing a create, update or resume whose restored state has an external recipient needs a fresh MFA. An interactive caller without one is answered 401 step-up-required and nothing changes (401 unauthenticated without a session, as everywhere); an API token or an automation is held for an approval that carries step-up (202, holdReason step_up, SX-4). The undo preview says so in stepUpRequired.

200.description: The undo operation; undoes names the operation it undid

ActiveDIQ-Operation-Id.description: The undo operation. Undoing it re-applies the original change.

202.description: The undo is held for approval by the gate or a kernel hold (ADR-0005 rule 8); holdReason says which: undo_needed_approval when the undone operation needed approval, step_up when a token or automation restores an external recipient (TM-D30 SX-1, SX-4). Nothing changed yet

post.description: The dry run of createReportSchedule as the Action reports.schedule.create (ADR-0004 rule 14): it plans the change against the live state, authorises it for the caller and asks the gate, and answers what the submit would do, the diff, reversibility, required confirmations and whether it can be undone. It writes, persists and audits nothing, and needs no step-up. A refusal the plan finds is a 200 with outcome refused and blocked[].code report_scope_empty, report_scope_unsupported, external_not_permitted or name_taken, never a problem; so is a gate denial. Same x-permission and body as createReportSchedule. Create has no target yet, so the 404 is that of the write (the definition is unknown or not visible).

delete.description: Deletes the schedule, as the Action reports.schedule.delete (ADR-0005 rule 10), with undo that restores it. Needs If-Match. Stored artefacts of earlier runs are kept until they expire. Preview it first with previewDeleteReportSchedule (same parameters, including If-Match; nothing is written). The ActiveDIQ-Operation-Id it answers is the undo handle for undoReportScheduleOperation.

202.description: Held for approval by the gate or a kernel hold (ADR-0005 rule 8); holdReason says which. This Action never steps up (TM-D30 SX-2), so it is never held step_up. Nothing changed yet; it applies when approved

ActiveDIQ-Operation-Id.description: The operation that made this change. It is the undo handle for undoReportScheduleOperation.

get.description: Answers one schedule with its recurrence, recipients and the delivery state of each recipient (E4), next run and last run. The ETag is the version to send as If-Match when changing it. Another owner's schedule is answered only with reports.schedule.manage_all (otherwise 404).

put.description: Replaces every writable setting, as the Action reports.schedule.update (ADR-0005 rule 10): preview diff against the current version, gate, audit, and undo that restores the previous version. Needs If-Match with the ETag read. The same external-recipient rule as create applies: reports.deliver.external guards the external case only, and the confirmation covers every external address that is new or changed. Changing another owner's schedule additionally needs reports.schedule.manage_all. The scope refusals of create apply. Preview it first with previewUpdateReportSchedule (same body and parameters; nothing is written). The ActiveDIQ-Operation-Id it answers is the undo handle for undoReportScheduleOperation.

ActiveDIQ-Operation-Id.description: The operation that made this change. It is the undo handle for undoReportScheduleOperation.

202.description: Held for approval by the gate or a kernel hold (ADR-0005 rule 8); holdReason says which, for example step_up when a token or automation makes a change whose after-state has an external recipient (TM-D30 SX-1, SX-4). Nothing changed yet; it applies when approved

put.description: Hands the schedule to another account, as the Action reports.schedule.reassign (ADR-0005 rule 10). This is the one schedule operation bound to reports.schedule.manage_all. The schedule pauses until the new owner resumes it, so a reassignment cannot widen what recipients receive without the new owner's act. The new owner must hold reports.run, reports.export and reports.schedule (400 with code owner_lacks_permission otherwise). Needs If-Match. Preview it first with previewReassignReportSchedule (same body and parameters; nothing is written). The ActiveDIQ-Operation-Id it answers is the undo handle for undoReportScheduleOperation.

200.description: The schedule, paused under its new owner

ActiveDIQ-Operation-Id.description: The operation that made this change. It is the undo handle for undoReportScheduleOperation.

202.description: Held for approval by the gate or a kernel hold (ADR-0005 rule 8); holdReason says which. This Action never steps up (TM-D30 SX-2), so it is never held step_up. Nothing changed yet; it applies when approved

post.description: Pauses the schedule, as the Action reports.schedule.pause (ADR-0005 rule 10). A paused schedule fires nothing until it is resumed. Pausing another owner's schedule additionally needs reports.schedule.manage_all. A pause the system makes under the owner-authority rule is not this operation; it is audited as an event and shows as pausedReason. Preview it first with previewPauseReportSchedule (same parameters; nothing is written). The ActiveDIQ-Operation-Id it answers is the undo handle for undoReportScheduleOperation.

ActiveDIQ-Operation-Id.description: The operation that made this change. It is the undo handle for undoReportScheduleOperation.

202.description: Held for approval by the gate or a kernel hold (ADR-0005 rule 8); holdReason says which. This Action never steps up (TM-D30 SX-2), so it is never held step_up. Nothing changed yet; it applies when approved

post.description: The dry run of deleteReportSchedule as the Action reports.schedule.delete (ADR-0004 rule 14): it plans the change against the live state, authorises it for the caller and asks the gate, and answers what the submit would do, the diff, reversibility, required confirmations and whether it can be undone. It writes, persists and audits nothing, and needs no step-up. This Action has no plan refusal of its own; a gate denial is a 200 with outcome refused, never a problem. Same x-permission and parameters (including If-Match) as deleteReportSchedule; it has no body. Same visibility (another owner's schedule is 404 without reports.schedule.manage_all).

The dry run of pauseReportSchedule as the Action reports.schedule.pause (ADR-0004 rule 14): it plans the change against the live state, authorises it for the caller and asks the gate, and answers what the submit would do, the diff, reversibility, required confirmations and whether it can be undone. It writes, persists and audits nothing, and needs no step-up. This Action has no plan refusal of its own: pausing a paused schedule is outcome no_change, and a gate denial is a 200 with outcome refused, never a problem. Same x-permission and parameters as pauseReportSchedule; it has no body. Same visibility (another owner's schedule is 404 without reports.schedule.manage_all).

The dry run of reassignReportSchedule as the Action reports.schedule.reassign (ADR-0004 rule 14): it plans the change against the live state, authorises it for the caller and asks the gate, and answers what the submit would do, the diff, reversibility, required confirmations and whether it can be undone. It writes, persists and audits nothing, and needs no step-up. A refusal the plan finds is a 200 with outcome refused and blocked[].code owner_lacks_permission, never a problem; so is a gate denial. Same x-permission, parameters (including If-Match) and body as reassignReportSchedule; its x-permission already is reports.schedule.manage_all.

The dry run of resumeReportSchedule as the Action reports.schedule.resume (ADR-0004 rule 14): it plans the change against the live state, authorises it for the caller and asks the gate, and answers what the submit would do, the diff, reversibility, required confirmations and whether it can be undone. It writes, persists and audits nothing, and needs no step-up. A refusal the plan finds is a 200 with outcome refused and blocked[].code owner_only, report_scope_empty or report_scope_unsupported, never a problem; so is a gate denial. Resuming an active schedule is outcome no_change. Same x-permission and parameters as resumeReportSchedule; it has no body. Same visibility (another owner's schedule is 404 without reports.schedule.manage_all).

The dry run of updateReportSchedule as the Action reports.schedule.update (ADR-0004 rule 14): it plans the change against the live state, authorises it for the caller and asks the gate, and answers what the submit would do, the diff, reversibility, required confirmations and whether it can be undone. It writes, persists and audits nothing, and needs no step-up. A refusal the plan finds is a 200 with outcome refused and blocked[].code report_scope_empty, report_scope_unsupported, external_not_permitted or name_taken, never a problem; so is a gate denial. Same x-permission, parameters (including If-Match) and body as updateReportSchedule, and the same visibility (another owner's schedule is 404 without reports.schedule.manage_all).

Resumes a paused schedule, as the Action reports.schedule.resume (ADR-0005 rule 10). Only the owner may, after seeing the recipient list; resuming re-checks the owner's scope, with the refusals of create. A reassigned schedule stays paused until its new owner does this. post.description: Fires the schedule once now, exactly as a scheduled fire: a run of the pinned definition under the owner's current scope and permissions, then delivery to each recipient, every external address re-evaluated against the current allowed domains. Answers the run. Only the schedule's owner may call this, because the run is the owner's and reports.schedule.manage_all never opens another owner's runs (modules/reports.md 6.6); anyone else, a manage_all holder included, gets 404. It is bookkeeping, not an Action. A per-DC schedule cannot be run now more often than daily (409). A schedule whose owner is disabled or has lost a permission is paused instead (409).

202.description: The run is accepted and queued

post.description: The first-run setup gate (TM-TB16-T7). A fresh install writes a one-time setup secret where only the installing administrator can read it (`activediq-server setup show`). Presenting it here claims setup: in one step the secret is consumed and the first tenant-owner account is created and granted the tenant-owner role (a failure creating the owner leaves the secret unconsumed). The secret never works again. The new account has no credential yet and cannot sign in until one is enrolled. Success answers 204 and no body. A second claim is refused like any other failure. Every failure has one shape, 401 /problems/setup-refused: wrong secret, expired secret, already-used secret, and an install that is not in first-run state are indistinguishable. The source-IP limiter may answer 429. No default account exists before or after.

204.description: Setup was claimed, the secret is consumed and the first tenant owner exists.
